title: Certificates of Deposit: Limits on How Many Certificates One Customer May Hold
content:
A customer may hold several Certificates of Deposit at Piedmont Crescent Bank at once, but the number is limited in two independent ways: across all tiers together, and within each single tier. Both limits are tested when a new certificate is to be opened.

## Governing clause

A new certificate may be opened only while both of the following hold, each read from the bank's own certificate records for that customer at the time of the opening:

- **Customer-wide limit.** The customer's certificates that are not closed number fewer than 20.
- **Per-tier limit.** The customer's certificates of the tier being requested that are not closed number fewer than that tier's limit in the table below.

A certificate counts toward both limits while it is in applied status (opened and awaiting its opening deposit), in active status, or in its grace period. A closed certificate never counts. If either count has already reached its limit, the opening is declined outright and no certificate is created.

## Per-tier limits

| Tier | Ceiling on open certificates of the tier, per customer |
|---|---|
| 6-Month Certificate | 5 |
| 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate | 2 |
| 12-Month Certificate | 5 |
| 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate | 3 |
| 36-Month Certificate | 5 |
| 60-Month Certificate | 5 |

## What is counted and whose records decide

| Question | Answer under this clause |
|---|---|
| Whose certificates are counted? | Those recorded under the customer who would own the new certificate. |
| Which record decides? | The certificate records the bank holds, not the customer's own tally. |
| Which tier is counted for the per-tier limit? | Only the tier named in the opening request. |
| Is a certificate awaiting funding counted? | Yes; applied status counts. |
| Is a certificate closed as unfunded counted? | No; closed certificates are never counted. |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical holdings)

- A customer with 19 certificates not closed, none of them 11-Month No-Penalty Certificates, asks for an 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate: the customer-wide count is below 20 and the tier count is below 2, so the opening may proceed.
- The same customer, now holding 20 certificates not closed, asks for any tier: the customer-wide limit has been reached and the opening is declined.
- A customer holding 3 open 18-Month Bump-Up Certificates and 2 closed ones asks for another of that tier: the three open ones already reach the tier limit of 3, so the opening is declined even though the customer-wide count is low.
